sn16.13:0.3: The Counterfeit of the True Dhamma
sn16.13:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Savatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anathapiṇḍika’s Park.
sn16.13:1.3: Then the Venerable Mahakassapa approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn16.13:1.4: “Venerable sir, what is the reason, what is the cause, why formerly there were fewer training rules but more bhikkhus were established in final knowledge,
sn16.13:1.5: while now there are more training rules but fewer bhikkhus are established in final knowledge?”
sn16.13:1.6: “That’s the way it is, Kassapa. When beings are deteriorating and the true Dhamma is disappearing there are more training rules but fewer bhikkhus are established in final knowledge.
sn16.13:1.7: Kassapa, the true Dhamma does not disappear so long as a counterfeit of the true Dhamma has not arisen in the world.
sn16.13:1.8: But when a counterfeit of the true Dhamma arises in the world, then the true Dhamma disappears.
sn16.13:2.1: “Just as, Kassapa, gold does not disappear so long as counterfeit gold has not arisen in the world,
sn16.13:2.2: but when counterfeit gold arises then true gold disappears,
sn16.13:2.3: so the true Dhamma does not disappear so long as a counterfeit of the true Dhamma has not arisen in the world,
sn16.13:2.4: but when a counterfeit of the true Dhamma arises in the world, then the true Dhamma disappears.
sn16.13:3.1: “It is not the earth element, Kassapa, that causes the true Dhamma to disappear, nor the water element, nor the heat element, nor the air element.
sn16.13:3.2: It is the senseless people who arise right here who cause the true Dhamma to disappear.
sn16.13:3.3: “The true Dhamma does not disappear all at once in the way a ship sinks.
sn16.13:4.1: There are, Kassapa, five detrimental things that lead to the decay and disappearance of the true Dhamma.
sn16.13:4.3: Here the bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs, the male lay followers, and the female lay followers dwell without reverence and deference towards the Teacher; they dwell without reverence and deference towards the Dhamma; they dwell without reverence and deference towards the Saṅgha; they dwell without reverence and deference towards the training; they dwell without reverence and deference towards concentration.
sn16.13:4.4: These, Kassapa, are the five detrimental things that lead to the decay and disappearance of the true Dhamma.
sn16.13:5.1: “There are five things, Kassapa, that lead to the longevity of the true Dhamma, to its nondecay and nondisappearance.
sn16.13:5.3: Here the bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs, the male lay followers, and the female lay followers dwell with reverence and deference towards the Teacher; they dwell with reverence and deference towards the Dhamma; they dwell with reverence and deference towards the Saṅgha; they dwell with reverence and deference towards the training; they dwell with reverence and deference towards concentration.
sn16.13:5.4: These, Kassapa, are the five things that lead to the longevity of the true Dhamma, to its nondecay and nondisappearance.”
